items.title: PDL-CAS-25-004, Options to Fill Vacant Council Position
notes:
William Short, Regional Clerk, provided a brief overview of report PDL-CAS-25-004, Options to Fill Vacant Council Position. He noted that Council was notified of the vacant Councillor-Kitchener position at the Council meeting on January 29, 2025 and that Council decided to defer their decision to March 4, 2025 in order to account for the results of the provincial election which was held on February 27, 2025. He highlighted that the report outlines the options for filling the vacant position either through appointment or by-election. The proposed appointment process outlines three options for Council to consider. The first option is to appoint the next candidate with the most votes for the Councillor-Kitchener position from the 2022 Municipal election. The second option is to accept applications from the public and make a selection from those submissions. And the third option was for Council to select a candidate directly.

Council discussed and deliberated the potential options provided in the Staff report. In response to Council, Tim Brubacher, Deputy Clerk/Manager of Council Services, confirmed that the previous vacancy of Regional Council in 2015 was filled by appointing the next candidate with the most votes from the previous Municipal election. He further confirmed that the previous Kitchener candidate, Matt Rodrigues, has verified that he is eligible and willing to serve. Staff would take the necessary steps to confirm the M. Rodrigues' qualifying address if Council were to appoint him. Several Council Members expressed support for appointing M. Rodrigues based on the precedent set for filling a vacancy, cost savings, and that the electorate had conveyed support for M. Rodrigues. T. Brubacher corroborated that M. Rodrigues had approximately 400 votes less than Councillor R. Deutschmann. W. Short noted the City of Kitchener Municipal Clerk has estimated that a by-election would cost approximately $800,000.

D. McCabe suggested that the appointment process through the submission of applications should be considered as there have been community changes since the 2022 election and the application process might provide opportunities for diverse applications. She also expressed concern that Matt Rodrigues is currently employed by one of the area municipalities. T. Brubacher explained the Municipal Act, 2001 does not prohibit employees of an area municipality to serve on Regional Council as well M. Rodrigues has indicated that he would take a voluntary leave of absence from the City of Kitchener during his time as a Councillor and would be connected with the Regional integrity commissioner to ensure there are no conflicts.

T. Brubacher proposed that the by-law to appoint M. Rodrigues to Regional Council be considered at the Special Council meeting on March 13, 2025 to begin his term as soon as is practical.
